1.0 INTRODUCTION:

1.1 To ensure uniform care of patients with all statutory compliances

2.0 SCOPE:

2.2 Health Care Providers

2.3 Patients

2.4 Government agencies

3.1 Doctors, Hospital Management

3.2 Nursing staff

4.1 AAC - Access Assessment and Continuity of Care

6.0 REFERENCE:

6.1 NABH: Accreditation Standards For Ayurveda Hospitals 2nd Edition April 2016.

7.0 OBJECTIVE ELEMENTS

7.1 The patient’s discharge process is planned in consultation with the patient and/or family.

7.2 Documented policies and procedures exist for coordination of various departments and agencies involved in the discharge process (including medicolegal and absconded cases).

7.3 Documented policies and procedures are in place for patients leaving against medical advice (LAMA) and patients being discharged on request.

7.4 A discharge summary is given to all the patients leaving the organization (including patients leaving against medical advice and on request).

8. 0 PROCESSES :-

8.1 The patient's treating doctor determines the readiness for discharge during regular reassessments. The same is discussed with the patient and family.

8.2 Discharge procedures shall be followed to ensure patients are discharged effectively and efficiently, allowing for optimal utilization of available resources.

8.2.1 An authorized hospital discharge shall only be made by an order from the primary consultant. However, a patient may discharge himself/herself against medical advice.

8.2.2 The Consultant or his designee shall document discharge instructions in the patient’s medical record at the time of anticipated discharge.

8.2.3 A Discharge Summary shall be prepared in standard format

8.2.4 The Ward Sister shall be the responsible person to ensure compliance with this policy.

8.2.5 The discharge summary shall contain:

• The reason for admission

• Significant findings

• Any diagnosis

• Procedures performed

• Significant medications administered

• Condition at discharge

• Discharge medications and follow-up instructions

8.2.7 In case of death, the discharge summary includes the cause of death

8.2.8 The nurse shall be responsible for completing the discharge checklist and explaining the discharge summary to the patient.

8.2.9 All the patients are provided with a discharge summary at the time of discharge including LAMA

8.2.10 Patients requesting discharge against medical advice shall be explained the risks and consequences. The consent will be obtained from the patient/ family as per the informed consent policy.

8.2.11 Hospital provides discharge summary to only IPD patients. one copy is given to the patient and one copy is retained in case sheet
